title: Electric Flux as a Criterion for String Breaking and Schwinger Pair Production
abstract: We define string breaking by the midpoint electric field falling to half a flux unit. In the massive Schwinger model, an energy balance between intact string and screened configuration predicts this separation using only vacuum observables and meson masses as input. We observe numerically that this half flux point corresponds to equal weights of the two configurations thus explaining the observed peak of the entanglement entropy as maximal uncertainty of the binary flux. The same binary uncertainty explains the entanglement peak at the vacuum transition. Near breaking, screening organizes part of the spatial entanglement between the string interior and exterior into a nearly maximally entangled bit. Within the selected flux sectors, this approximate encoded Bell pair records whether the flux is screened and nearly separates from the remaining correlations. The vacuum transition exhibits the same structure. The string and the $θ$-vacuum reveal a matching structure of the capacity of entanglement minimum at their transition point, linking their entanglement spectra. The transition rearranges degrees of freedom coherently as revealed by the entanglement asymmetry and Robustness of Magic of disjoint subregions. Finally, we construct the $θ$-vacuum and string wavefunctions with high fidelity using a restricted Boltzmann machine ansatz.
summary: This work establishes electric flux as the key diagnostic for string breaking and Schwinger pair production in the massive Schwinger model. By analyzing entanglement entropy, the authors show that the point of string breaking corresponds to a maximum in entanglement, linking this process to the vacuum transition structure. The methodology combines lattice field theory simulations with quantum information measures.
main_problem: The paper investigates string breaking and Schwinger pair production, using the electric flux as a fundamental criterion for these non-perturbative quantum field theory processes.
main_result: String breaking is characterized by the midpoint electric field falling to half a flux unit, which corresponds to a maximum in the entanglement entropy, linking it to vacuum transition physics.
method: The study employs numerical calculations using Hamiltonian lattice formulations (Matrix Product States) and analytic solutions derived from minimizing energy functionals in the massive Schwinger model.
model_or_system: The primary model is the massive Schwinger model (QED in 1+1 dimensions), used as a minimal realization of confinement, involving static external charges and a $\theta$-angle background.
key_observables: Electric Flux ($E$), String Potential ($V(d)$), Entanglement Entropy, and the order parameter $\text{Ein}(d)$ for string breaking.
important_parameters: The flux unit (1), the fermion mass ($m$), the external charge ($q$), and the $\theta$-angle.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on extending descriptions perturbatively to first order in the fermion mass, and uses the massive Schwinger model as the physical proxy for confinement.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the electric flux diagnostic ($	ext{Ein}(d)$) showing the transition point, and show the spatial dependence of charge coherence across the string structure.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by defining the flux criterion, calculating the energy balance in the massive Schwinger model, analyzing entanglement entropy peaks at the half-flux point, and finally comparing the structure of the vacuum transition to string breaking.
why_interesting: The deep connection drawn between entanglement structure (entanglement entropy peaks) and fundamental non-perturbative phenomena like string breaking provides a powerful quantum information diagnostic tool for strongly coupled field theories.

The gray dashed curve is the massless free-boson result Eq. (15). The colored dashed curve at m/g = 0.025 incorporates the first-order mass cor- rection. The horizontal line identifies Ein = 1/2. Increasing m/g yields a convex region in gd that leads to a plateau at m/g followed by a sharp transition. The inset shows the cur- vature R of Eq. (17) for the light masses. Negative curvature indicates the developing concave region and is an imprint of the formation and breaking of the flux tube.

FIG. 3. Static-light pair energy MH and neutral vacuum me- son mass Ms, at ga = 1/8. The inset shows their difference ∆H = MH−Ms. Black squares give the exact massless values. The initial rise of ∆H is fixed by Eq. (21), while its shallow maximum near m/g = 0.2 is a numerical result.
FIG. 2. Discharge width and gap minimum as a function of m/g. Main: width-to-separation ratio W/(gdbreak). Inset: Relative separation of the location of the gap minimum d∗ and dbreak.

FIG. 4. Comparison of dbreak (points) and the screened en- ergy crossing dx (curve), Eq. (38), at ga = 1/8. The vac- uum susceptibility, meson mass and static-light plateau fix the curve independently. The open triangle is the analytic m →0+ limit of dx, distinct from dbreak(0). The inset compares σ = 2π2χtop with the mass-based prediction σM, Eq. (31) and the slope σV of the approximately linear part of the static potential. The latter is shown only for m/g ≥0.3, where this linear part can be resolved.

Figure 4 compares this energy crossing with dbreak ob- tained from the midpoint electric field. The agreement is excellent for all masses considered. Note that the in- puts are determined independently of that separation: Ms and σ come from vacuum calculations and MH from the static potential at large separation. The agreement with dbreak connects the local loss of flux to the energetic competition between an intact string with the screened configuration. Where the potential contains a resolved linear interval, its slope provides a separate test of the bulk coefficient, shown in the inset of Fig. 4.
